constraints: Offline immutable bytes, at most 65536 bytes and depth eight; existing canonical ASCII/safe-integer v1 profile, all rows validated, zero to sixteen peers.
External authenticated digest pin, local software-domain alias, trusted UTC and revision/time floors. Admit a valid empty deny-all table without invoking bundle or signature verification.
Return bounded immutable metadata with authority and qualification false. No I/O, enrollment, durable floors, implicit clock or new cryptographic protocol.
Portable desktop library boundary; no identified embedded target, WCET, memory budget or throughput SLA. Preserve existing federation bundle outcomes.
alternatives: Python lexical JSON hooks, immutable bytes and native-backed SHA-256 using the shared v1 validator.
Erlang/Elixir OTP JSON object/number callbacks with immutable binaries.
C#/F# Utf8JsonReader token spans with explicit duplicate and canonical-profile checks.
Rust serde_json custom visitor/raw-token handling and immutable borrowed input.
rationale: KEEP the bounded lexical validator for this additive API: callbacks preserve duplicate keys and numeric spellings before conversion, and the exact immutable input remains stable through canonical equality and digest comparison.

OTP callbacks and native token readers are credible alternatives outside the incumbent language. None inherently supplies the canonical profile, complete-table validation or externally trusted pins. Sharing the actual v1 validator prevents a second acceptance policy; merely selecting another runtime does not supply a demonstrated resource or trust benefit here.

Expose snapshot admission separately from peer/bundle acceptance so deny-all metadata is available to a future floor store even when no bundle can succeed. Existing bundle verification is unchanged; portable cases and negative boundary tests must establish parity of overlapping gates.

No alternative runtime was executed or benchmarked, and no latency superiority is inferred. Reopen selection for measured native/embedded constraints; installed tooling, familiarity and rewrite cost do not justify this choice.
limits: Validation is not transport authentication, key enrollment, authorization, storage or same-revision equivocation detection. Pins and time must be independently trusted.
All peer metadata is checked, but referenced policy bytes and signatures are not fetched or validated. Empty peers is valid denial of all peers, not a grant.
No hard-real-time, hardware, MLS/CNSA, availability, tactical or customer-product qualification. Existing wire bounds are unchanged.
